item.title: How to Properly Define C Function Signatures in Python's `ctypes`?
item.description:
When interacting with shared libraries (like .dll or .so files) using Python’s ctypes module, accurately defining the argument types and return type of the C functions is crucial. Failing to do so can lead to unexpected behavior, data corruption, and misleading error messages, particularly in 64-bit environments where data truncation can occur.

The ctypes module provides a foreign function library that allows Python code to call functions residing in C shared libraries. To ensure seamless data exchange between Python and C, you must explicitly specify the expected data types.
